papers.gist: A single-season tricot trial with 372 Tanzanian farmers finds yield, market preference and disease resistance drive bean choice, with zone-, gender- and youth-specific trait priorities
papers.keywords: common bean, Tanzania, tricot, trait preferences, gender, youth, anthracnose, market preference, intercropping, cooking with banana, red mottled, sugar bean, TARI, PVS

relations.note: common bean case study interview
women and men prioritize different traits in tricot trials of Tanzanian legumes

papers.not_established: that men are more involved than women in bean production nationally (participation shares come from one trial sample); effects across seasons (single season); measured yield or disease differences (yield was ranked by grain volume, disease by field-agent scores); that tricot data alone yield the detailed trait evaluations of PVS

papers.gist: Three long-running participatory breeding programmes show that farmer participation spread through champions and partnerships, while national seed and research policies lag far behind established practice
papers.keywords: Farmer First, participatory research, institutionalization, agricultural policy, seed systems, farmer organizations, quality-declared seed, variety release, champions, curricula, PABRA, CIAL

relations.note: cites tricot as digitally mediated crowdsourcing of varietal feedback

papers.not_established: that participatory breeding improved farmer welfare or food security in these cases (not assessed); that the three cases represent all countries; causal effects of the projects on policy (the authors draw lessons, not causal links); anything about tricot specifically, which is mentioned only as a form of crowdsourcing
